issues.legal_issue: Allegations of fraud do not make a dispute non-arbitrable when the arbitration agreement was executed and the dispute has no public overtones.
material_facts: The claimant alleged that the assignment and confirmation documents were procured by misrepresentation and concealment concerning a partner’s role and authority.
The claimant did not allege that the assignment agreement or confirmation deed had never been entered into.
The dispute was between the parties to the agreements and did not involve public overtones.
issues.conclusion: The fraud allegations did not oust the arbitrator’s jurisdiction, and the dispute was arbitrable.
issues.legal_principle: Following Avitel Post Studioz Limited v. HSBC PI Holding (Mauritius) Ltd., the Court held that fraud within section 17 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and fraud in performance amounting to the civil wrong of deceit, are arbitrable. Criminal overtones alone do not make a dispute non-arbitrable. The fraud exception does not apply on these facts; if the agreement itself had never been executed, the arbitration clause would not exist. The Court held that N. Radhakrishnan v. Maestro Engineers no longer had precedential force, and distinguished State of A.P. v. T. Suryachandra Rao as irrelevant to the issue.

rule.if: arbitration_referral_proceeding and arbitration_clause_in_executed_agreement and fraud_dispute_is_between_parties and not agreement_execution_denied and not dispute_has_public_overtones

predicates.arbitration_referral_proceeding: A party asked a judicial authority to refer a civil dispute to arbitration.
predicates.arbitration_clause_in_executed_agreement: The parties entered into an agreement containing a clause to arbitrate disputes within its scope.
predicates.fraud_dispute_is_between_parties: The alleged fraud concerns the rights and conduct of parties to the agreement.
predicates.agreement_execution_denied: A party asserted that the agreement containing the arbitration clause was never entered into.
predicates.dispute_has_public_overtones: The dispute has ramifications beyond the parties, rather than being confined to their private rights.

issues.definition: When a dispute referred for arbitration arises under an executed arbitration agreement, concerns the parties’ private rights, and does not involve public overtones, fraud allegations do not make it non-arbitrable if execution of the agreement is not denied.

issues.legal_issue: A judicial authority must refer a dispute to arbitration when the statutory conditions for referral are met unless it finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists.
material_facts: The claimant brought a civil suit seeking declarations and cancellation of agreements and a confirmation deed.
The opposing party applied for referral to arbitration under the clause in the assignment agreement.
The claimant acknowledged that the agreement containing the clause existed, while contending that it was affected by fraud.
The documents sought to be cancelled were not alleged never to have been entered into.
issues.conclusion: A valid arbitration agreement existed prima facie, so the referral to arbitration was proper.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as amended in 2015, a judicial authority before which an action is brought must refer the parties to arbitration if the other statutory conditions are met, unless it finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists. The Court relied on Ameet Lalchand Shah v. Rishabh Enterprises, Mayavati Trading Pvt. Ltd. v. Pradyut Deb Burman, Emaar MGF Land Ltd. v. Aftab Singh, and its reasoning in Avitel Post Studioz Limited v. HSBC PI Holding (Mauritius) Ltd. It noted the change from section 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940.

predicates.judicial_action_with_reference_request: A civil action was brought before a judicial authority and a party requested referral to arbitration.
predicates.prima_facie_valid_arbitration_agreement: The material before the judicial authority showed an apparently valid arbitration agreement governing the dispute, and the agreement was not shown never to have been entered into.

issues.definition: When a civil action is before a judicial authority and the available material shows an apparently valid arbitration agreement governing the dispute, the parties must be referred to arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: A claim to cancel a written instrument under the specific-relief cancellation remedy is an action in personam and is not non-arbitrable merely because the instrument is registered.
material_facts: The claimant sought declarations that written agreements and a confirmation deed were void and not binding, along with their cancellation.
The claim concerned the parties’ dealings and rights under those documents, not an adjudication binding the world at large.
The claimant was a party to the relevant assignment documents, and the suit did not present a dispute involving public rights.
The claimant argued that registration and the direction to notify the registration officer made cancellation a proceeding in rem.
issues.conclusion: A cancellation action of this kind is in personam and can be referred to arbitration; registration does not change that character. The Court overruled the contrary reasoning in Aliens Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. M. Janardhan Reddy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, provides a discretionary remedy to a person against whom a written instrument is void or voidable and who reasonably apprehends serious injury if it remains outstanding. The action is confined to parties to the instrument and persons who can derive title through them, and determines their rights inter se. Section 31(2), which requires a copy of a cancellation decree to be sent to the registration officer for notation, provides for a ministerial step after judgment and does not turn the action into one in rem. Section 4 of the Act confines specific relief to individual civil rights; sections 26, 27, and 29–35 support the in-personam character of the relevant remedies. The Court relied on Olympus Superstructures v. Meena Vijay Khetan to hold that civilly justiciable disputes, including specific-performance disputes, may be arbitrated; on Booz Allen & Hamilton Inc. v. SBI Home Finance Ltd. and R. Viswanathan v. Rukn-ul-Mulk Syed Abdul Wajid concerning in rem and in personam actions; on Muppudathi Pillai v. Krishnaswami Pillai and Mohd. Noorul Hoda v. Bibi Raifunnisa concerning the persons entitled to seek cancellation; and on Gopal Das v. Sri Thakurji, Razia Begum v. Sahebzadi Anwar Begum, Satrucharla Vijaya Rama Raju v. Nimmaka Jaya Raju, and Suhrid Singh v. Randhir Singh. The Court rejected Aliens Developers because registration does not give an otherwise private instrument a higher legal status, and the cancellation decree binds parties and their privies rather than all persons generally.

predicates.written_instrument_cancellation_proceedi: A claimant seeks adjudication and cancellation of a written instrument said to be void or voidable and potentially injurious if left outstanding.
predicates.instrument_claim_affects_claimant_throug: The instrument was made by the claimant or by someone capable of binding the claimant, or the claimant derives title through such a person.
predicates.adjudication_is_limited_to_parties_and_p: The requested determination concerns the rights of the litigants and persons claiming through them, not the rights of everyone generally.
predicates.arbitration_agreement_covers_dispute: The parties have an arbitration agreement covering the dispute over the instrument.

issues.definition: A written-instrument cancellation dispute is in personam and arbitrable when it concerns an instrument affecting the claimant through a party, seeks a determination limited to the parties and their privies, and falls within their arbitration agreement.
